body:
The Native checkpoint prefix-reuse checkpoint is fully qualified on source d4d7b6535be2cf491b7859cacea2a9ada4ac8d9e.

[CI run 43664490758, attempt 1](https://github.com/nashspence/riverhog/actions/runs/43664490758) tested merge 05abffaef7f87a93b4949fcd6981e4ce6d033864. Every required check passed: 31 actual jobs across 26 workloads, with all original jobs stopped. The receiving owner verified 7,579 selected supplemental case IDs from exact worker artifacts and received the source-owned raw growth evidence: 48 scoped witnesses, 54 executions, 1,219 top-level samples. These scoped witnesses do not close whole-path G10/G12/G13 acceptance.

The implementation reuses the parsed prefix state only inside the same fresh Native storage observation. Fresh SQL, current source/worker/algorithm/prefix/predecessor authority, canonical validation, transaction/CAS, and the independent publication-selected-prefix parse remain. Pinned lint and 107 focused owner cases passed locally, including nine new warm-read corruption/rejection cases; original exits and cleanup were received.

The exact-input three-history diagnostic retained all 479 semantic progress/control traces, DBAPI attempts, source deliveries and materialized outputs. PrefixState parses fell from 5,185 to 3,758; all 1,903 ValidationCheckpoint parses remain. No timing speedup is claimed from these diagnostic lanes.

The remaining cost questions stay open. Offline inspection places all 418 historical catalog raises in finalization, but the original recorder omitted exception types/codes, statement families and retry identity; the data cannot classify their cause or isolate their cost. Correction-wide work, transaction costs, transport lifetimes and actual ready-key/worker occupancy are not cleared. This CI PostgreSQL suite alone took 8,109.70 seconds for 1,171 tests; that is a timing observation, not a growth-regression conclusion. Its retained artifacts contain aggregate target timing, without per-case durations or CPU/worker occupancy. Per-case attribution of this backend cost remains an open #991 evidence gap.

Next implementation awaits the focused bounded-Core-stepping [design/reference request](https://github.com/nashspence/riverhog/issues/991#issuecomment-6887528297), including explicit step/work/resource limits, freshness, durable error ordering, fairness and original receiving. Native phase fusion, commit removal or changed concurrency are outside that request's initial scope. The full small-journal caller census and 1,000/10,000/100,000-member campaigns remain held; this checkpoint does not trigger a rerun.

Complete-evidence SHA-256: 506fb42748405f9af273efb633b6e036fc1d2b0f1f0fd1fe87753144ac845490.

Received the [bounded-Core-stepping handoff 6889755494](https://github.com/nashspence/riverhog/issues/991#issuecomment-6889755494), exact reference 46ace062078d08cd70f508a3f3a7d834a92cbb40 on sole parent d4d7b6535be2cf491b7859cacea2a9ada4ac8d9e. All 13 manifest entries, 47 distinct tracked source pins, 12 subtree relationships, the exact two-file prefix delta and both context comments reconciled. Product paths outside the reference packet are identical; receiving ran no product calls or tests.

Decision: retain the current one-step runtime and per-step catalog adoption. Static source review confirms that ordinary Native certificate checks do not cover the completed rank graph-result predicate. Final-only adoption also needs a different partial-progress protocol when an earlier Native commit is followed by capacity or a later catalog conflict. The conservative alternative preserves those checks but establishes only possible intermediate stamp savings while changing scheduler/finalization opportunities; that does not presently justify a new coordination boundary. A fresh preparation-readiness validator remains separate owning research if pursued.

Current d4d7 source remains fully qualified. This closes the immediate grouping proposal, not #991, #964 or G10/G12/G13 acceptance.

Next independent analysis is one tiny F1/C1/K2/Q1 publication diagnostic: one 65,536-byte member, ordinary retained journals, a 120-second finalization deadline and a finite 4 GiB scratch-disk lease. It extends the existing recorder with bounded exception type/database-code, parameter-free SQL structure identity, owning scope and failed-attempt interval records. Meaningful actual-SQL self-checks must preserve missing-column and nonwaiting writer-refusal errors before the profile can run. Fresh/warm/evicted reader verification and original helper/scratch receiving remain required.

This addresses the missing catalog-error details; transport/transaction cost, correction-wide work and actual ready-key/worker occupancy remain open. The full caller census and aggressive member-scale campaigns stay held. No product runtime change, CI rerun, throughput claim, merge, release or provider activation.

### Received catalog-error diagnostic

On fully qualified source d4d7b6535be2cf491b7859cacea2a9ada4ac8d9e, one ordinary F1/C1/K2/Q1 publication completed with one 65,536-byte member. Publication took 36.315 seconds; the complete helper took 49.217 seconds. Fresh/warm/evicted Native readers verified the archive after source/upload scratch removal. Actual helper/driver/lease exits and cleanup were received; the product checkout stayed clean. The recorded finalization deadline was 120 seconds. No matching measured reference or throughput comparison is claimed.

The recorder received 51,811 catalog execute attempts and all 465 raised attempts. Every raised attempt was sqlite3.OperationalError, SQLITE_BUSY (5), at the exact parameter-free statement BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The count reconciles to the independent per-thread span buckets. Failed-attempt intervals summed to 18.410 ms wall / 12.768 ms thread CPU, ending at entry to SQLAlchemy's error callback. These intervals exclude subsequent retry, connection, coordination, rollback and receiving work; their sum is not a concurrent critical path. The 302 failures under producer.finish and 163 without an instrumented parent scope do not establish caller ownership or retry policy. This run's 465 errors cannot retroactively supply the missing metadata of the historical 418.

Actual missing-column and nonwaiting writer-refusal self-checks preserved SQL error identities, return/BaseException behavior, generator use and original resource/thread receiving before publication ran. Raw diagnostic SHA-256: 5da872016fae26039c92c53d36ec3281374e71b2b8475281cca72d55b8187390. Profile SHA-256: bdee7c0313e257933888f0fc6058e8387def8c30c1e5f44c3256897d8bd5ee6a.

### Focused reference request: actual ready work and worker occupancy

The [Core-stepping decision](https://github.com/nashspence/riverhog/issues/991#issuecomment-6889902338) retains one-step execution and per-step catalog adoption after receiving reference 46ace062078d08cd70f508a3f3a7d834a92cbb40. Please provide a focused source/evidence reference for the remaining #991 parallelization question: is independently eligible work actually delayed while usable execution capacity is idle, and where does the owning scheduling/resource boundary place that delay?

Start from exact d4d7. Reconcile the existing source and retained findings before any execution. Distinguish the ordinary Core route, the maintained fixture's SDK/coordinator opportunities, selected-journal HTTP opportunities and application lifespan workers. Two retained slots do not mean a two-thread executor. Entering TestClient starts additional reapers and must not be treated as a neutral transport change.

Define an observable ready/admissible key from fresh owner authority, not a saved ready boolean or an unclassified candidate row. Correlate exact source/attempt, readiness, admission/refusal, actual execution entry/exit, original worker/future and resource receiving with bounded monotonic records. Distinguish dependency ordering, busy keys, full retained capacity, unknown originals, writer admission and actual executor occupancy. If possible, attribute the two observed catalog-refusal caller families and their dispositions without recording SQL parameters, error messages or private deployment identity.

Use static/retained evidence first. If actual observation is necessary, limit it to a maintained tiny fixture with two genuinely independent journal keys and a few existing Core/Native turns under one approximately 120-second cooperative workload cap. Preserve ordinary per-step budgets, readiness checks, Native phases/transactions, catalog adoption, finalization opportunities and original resource ownership. Receive every actual original and remove scratch. An incomplete bounded trace is partial evidence; a timeout or cancellation request is not receipt of an entered operation. If the maintained fixture cannot supply the required independent readiness within that scope, report the specific source/design gap instead of expanding into a campaign.

Provide lossless bounded raw records and an offline reconciler for actual queue/admission/start/receive intervals where executed, exact source/probe pins, lifetime/resource and growth-composition limits, and a narrow conclusion about demonstrated avoidable serialization or the evidence still missing. Attribute prior receiving reports as reports, not newly rerun validation. Source analysis may justify a negative result; no runtime optimization is required.

Keep this focused on measurement and owning responsibility. No grouped stepping, skipped guards, deferred adoption, phase fusion, removed commits, changed production concurrency, full publication campaign, full caller census, broad suites or 1,000+ trials. No G10/G12/G13 closure, all-cost non-growth clearance or timing acceptance gate follows from the result. Use the external-reference convention, manifest/source hashes and a handoff citing this request.
